sections.category: Anthropic ships Claude Sonnet 5, a mid-tier model tuned for cheaper autonomous agents at near-Opus quality

bullets.body: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5 on June 30, positioning its refreshed midsize model as the cheapest way to run long-horizon agents at close to flagship quality. The pitch is explicitly agentic: the model is built to make plans and use tools like browsers and terminals and to run autonomously at a level that a few months ago required larger, more expensive models, with Anthropic claiming a substantial jump over Sonnet 4.6 (February) on reasoning, tool use, coding, and knowledge work and cost-performance parity with Opus 4.8 on the BrowseComp agentic-search and OSWorld-Verified computer-use benchmarks at medium-to-high effort. Pricing lands at an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through August 31, then steps up to a standard $3/$15; Sonnet 5 is the default model on Free and Pro and is available to Max, Team, and Enterprise as well as the API. Anthropic also flags a safety angle relevant to the agent-security thread of recent weeks: the model shows a lower rate of undesirable behaviors and is better at refusing malicious requests and resisting hijack attempts in prompt-injection attacks than its predecessor (9to5Mac). The read-through is that per-token cost for capable agentic work keeps falling from the mid-tier, which is where the enterprise token bills that Gartner has been flagging actually accumulate.

sections.category: Anthropic launches Claude Science, an agent harness that wires the existing Claude models into 60+ scientific databases and lab tools

bullets.body: On the same June 30 cycle Anthropic also shipped Claude Science, a research workbench that is notably not a new model but a harness: it runs the same Claude models already on sale (including Opus 4.8, with no special access) and adds pre-configured connectors to more than 60 scientific databases and computation tools spanning genomics, single-cell, proteomics, structural biology, and cheminformatics. Like Claude Code, it is designed to carry out meaningful work from concise high-level instructions, automating biology and chemistry tasks such as predicting protein structures and mapping a research field end to end (Let's Data Science). Availability is immediate for all paid subscribers, and Anthropic paired the launch with an AI-for-Science program funding up to 50 projects with as much as $30,000 in compute credits each (Modal adding up to $2,000 for selected projects), applications open through July 15 and projects running September to December. The interesting structural signal for the harness / workflow-orchestration topic is that the differentiated product is the tool-integration layer and domain skills around a general model, not the weights themselves — the same code-agent-harness pattern extended from software into wet-lab science.

sections.category: A cluster of critical RCE CVEs in agentic-AI developer tooling lands in late June, with Flowise's custom-MCP command-injection scored 9.9

bullets.body: The AI-security surface most exercised right now is the open-source agent-builder tooling itself, not the models. A June 23 advisory disclosed CVE-2026-56274, a CVSS 9.9 OS-command-injection flaw in Flowise's Custom MCP Server feature (versions before 3.1.2): incomplete command-flag validation plus a regex bypass in local-file-access restrictions let any authenticated user configure a malicious MCP server that slips past the validateCommandFlags blocklist and runs arbitrary host commands such as docker build or npx --yes. It is one of a wider late-June wave of remote-code-execution flaws in AI/ML development frameworks — Crawl4AI (CVE-2026-53753), Langflow, and picklescan all carried CVSS scores in the 9.6-9.8 range in the same window. Separately, a code-execution weakness in Microsoft AutoGen Studio (disclosed June 23) stems from insufficient containerization, so agent-generated code executes in the host process context with excessive privileges and escapes the intended sandbox — the same seven-day window that also saw a Mastra AI prompt-injection-to-RCE reportedly exploited by the Lazarus Group and a LiteLLM SSRF/deserialization flaw added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The common thread is the MCP-server / tool-execution boundary: the plumbing that lets agents call tools is where the exploitable code is concentrating.

sections.category: Fresh arxiv work on orchestrating agents pushes the agentic-workflow research front the same week

bullets.body: New research submitted to arXiv on June 29 keeps the multi-agent orchestration topic moving. "Design and Implementation of Agentic Orchestrations and Orchestration of Agents" (2606.31518) by Stefanie Rinderle-Ma and co-authors takes the coordination problem head-on, treating how agents are composed and orchestrated as the first-order engineering concern rather than an afterthought bolted onto individual agents. The same day brought "A Self-Evolving Agentic System for Automated Generation and Execution of Biological Protocols" (2606.31763) by Yankai Jiang and colleagues, an autonomous system that generates and runs lab protocols and adapts over time — a research-side echo of the wet-lab agent-harness direction Anthropic productized on June 30. Together with a plant-phenotyping agentic framework (2606.31831) posted the same day, the June 29 batch shows the literature converging on orchestration and self-evolving autonomy in domain-specific scientific settings, which is exactly where the commercial harness products are now aiming.

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: AI Engineer World's Fair is in its final two days in San Francisco, with summer and fall chip and security dates locked

bullets.body: The forward calendar across all three sub-tracks, refreshed as of July 1. Mainstream dev/data: the AI Engineer World's Fair at Moscone West in San Francisco is in its final stretch (running through July 2; ~29 tracks, ~300 speakers, 6,000+ attendees), with the Autoresearch keynote and ~12 parallel tracks today (July 1) and the Harness Engineering keynote closing it out July 2; further out, GitHub Universe returns October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas. AI-security: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay; Black Hat USA 2026 brings its AI Summit plus the main Briefings to Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas in early August, with DEF CON 34 and its AI Village the same week; OWASP Global AppSec USA is November 5-6 in San Francisco; and Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series (its San Francisco stop having run May 27) continues to Tokyo, London, and NYC, so it stays on the watch list. AI-chip/hardware: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is July 22-23 at Moscone (Instinct MI400-series focus on July 23), Hot Chips 2026 runs August 23-25 at Stanford's Memorial Auditorium, and the AI Infra Summit is September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center. Treat this bullet as an attendance planner: the security and chip tracks are where the agent-tooling-CVE and secure-AI-accelerator threads from recent weeks will surface in person.
